title: Concurrent lane scheduler and short-circuit timebox for reranker endpoint
creator: Maya Patel
description: Reduce P99 tail latency and improve throughput for the /v1/rerank endpoint under mixed token distributions by introducing a concurrent lane scheduler, per-lane microbatching, and a short-circuit timebox/EarlyExit policy. This ticket covers design, runtime changes to the reranker service, tests, and staged rollout with telemetry and rollback hooks.
acceptance_criteria: P99 for heavy tail workloads (tokenized length distribution with 80th/95th/99th percentiles) must improve by >= 25% compared to current baseline on dedicated staging cluster
No increase in error rate (>0.1% absolute) and correctness (rank-order A/B eval) within 1% of baseline for top-5 reranking quality
Feature gated and controllable via runtime flags: lane count, per-lane token cap, timebox_ms, speculative_batch_threshold
Automated load tests and canary plan in place with dashboard and alerting runbooks
All new code covered by unit and integration tests; end-to-end perf test reproducible in CI and on staging GPU nodes
implementation_summary: Introduce request classification into fast/short/long lanes based on token estimate; maintain per-lane microbatch queues with independent timeboxes and size caps. Use speculative microbatching to kick off small batches for short lanes and hedge long lanes by spawning a second faster (lower-accuracy) model variant when timebox approaches. Implement short-circuit early-exit in scorer when confidence delta between top candidates exceeds configurable threshold, avoiding full token decode for all candidates.
design_tradeoffs: Complexity: added scheduler and lane bookkeeping increases runtime state; mitigated via clear encapsulated scheduler module and comprehensive tests
Quality vs Latency: speculative lower-precision variant may slightly change ranking; will limit to candidate subsets and fallback to full model for high-stakes requests
Resource utilization: per-lane sizing may fragment GPU utilization under bursty mixed workloads; will tune adaptive lane sizing and allow autoscaler hints
benchmarks_baseline: Baseline measured on staging: p50=45ms, p95=210ms, p99=540ms under mixed distribution (30% short, 50% medium, 20% long), sustained qps=180 on 4xA10 pool
Quality baseline: top-5 MRR on internal rerank eval set = 0.842
benchmarks_target: Target: p99 <= 405ms (>=25% reduction), p95 <= 160ms, maintain or improve p50 and throughput >= 180 qps
Quality target: top-5 MRR drop <= 0.01 absolute; prefer no-drop
benchmark_results: Phase 1 prototype (lane=3, timebox_ms=[20,60,120], speculative_threshold=8): p50=42ms, p95=155ms, p99=390ms, qps +8% on same nodes
Phase 1 notes: short-circuit reduced compute by ~18% on short lanes; hedging reduced tail events from long lanes by 32%
rollout_plan: Stage 0: internal canary (10% traffic) for non-critical customers - 48h validation
Stage 1: incremental ramp to 50% over 72h if p99 improvement confirmed and error delta <0.05%
Stage 2: full rollout to hosted API with release notes and opt-out for Dedicated customers
Immediate rollback path: disable lane_scheduler flag and clear per-node queues; autoscaler will drain microbatches
telemetry_and_dashboards: New metrics: rerank.lane.* (queue_length, avg_batch_size, time_waited_ms), rerank.short_circuit.rate, rerank.speculative_fallback.count
Telemetry queries: SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 99) FROM rerank WHERE lane='long' AND time > now()-1h
test_plan: Unit tests for scheduler state transitions and per-lane backpressure
Integration: end-to-end rerank with KV cache warm/cold scenarios
Perf CI: reproduce benchmark harness with 4xA10 equivalent emulator; nightly runs and compare to baseline
Chaos test: kill a reranker worker mid-microbatch to ensure graceful retries and no duplicate scoring
updates: 2026-02-25: Kickoff - design session with Research, Infra, and Console. Agreed on 3-lane starting point and early-exit heuristic (delta-score threshold + min-processed-candidates).
2026-03-02: Prototype merged to feature branch; initial synthetic benchmarks show p99 improvement on mixed workloads. Documented candidate fallback rules.
2026-03-08: Integration PR for metrics and rollout flags opened. Console team added runtime toggles in feature flags UI.

2026-03-12: Canary started at 10% traffic with internal beta customers. Observed one class of requests (many small candidates with high token variance) where short-circuit triggers prematurely; reverted heuristic and added min-candidates threshold.
